title: Traces in the ground
goal: Make confident and cautious guesses about the past with -mIş olmalı, -mIş olabilir and -mIş olamaz.

intro.text: To guess about the past, put *olmalı* (must) or *olabilir* (may) after `-mIş`: *Burada yaşamış olmalılar* (They must have lived here), *Kaybolmuş olabilir* (It may have got lost). *Olamaz* rules a guess out. The person ending always goes on the last word.

vocab.en: belonging to (after the dative: bir çocuğa ait)

exercises.question: Ayşe's coat is on the chair and her tea is still warm. Which sentence draws the right conclusion?

why.1: *Gelmeliydi* is **she should have come** (B1 unit 2): a reproach, not a conclusion.
why.2: *Gelmeli* is **she should come**, or **she should be here soon**.
why.3: *Gelmiş olamaz* rules it out: **she can't have come**. The coat and the tea say the opposite.

exercises.explain: `-mIş olmalı` is a confident guess about the past, drawn from clues: **she must have come**.

exercises.text: Kemikler çok eski. Buraya yaklaşık dokuz bin yıl önce gömülmüş ___.
exercises.en: The bones are very old. They must have been buried here about nine thousand years ago.

reject.why: *Olmalıydı* makes it **should have been**: a criticism, not a guess.
*Olabilir* is **may have been**; the sentence says **must**.

exercises.explain: Passive *gömül-* (be buried) + `-mIş` + *olmalı*: **must have been buried**. A plural that isn't people, *kemikler*, keeps the verb singular.

reject.why: *Yaşamalılar* is **they must live here**: an obligation, or a guess about now. For the past, use `-mIş olmalı`.
*Yaşamalıydılar* is **they should have lived here** (B1 unit 2).

accept: Hunters may have made these tools.
Hunters might have made these tools.
Hunters could have made these tools.
The hunters [may have|might have|could have|might've|could've] made these tools.
These tools [may have|might have|could have] been made by (the) hunters.
It [may have|might have|could have] been (the) hunters who made these tools.
exercises.explain: *Avcılar* stands right before the verb, in the focus slot: the guess is about **who** made them.

exercises.title: Kazı günlüğü
exercises.passage:
Bugün güney açmasında bir evin tabanını temizledik. Taban, toprağın yaklaşık bir metre altındaydı. Tabanın altından küçük bir mezar çıktı. Kemikler çok küçük; bir çocuğa ait olmalı. Yanında taştan bir boncuk ve iki küçük alet vardı. Bu insanlar ölülerini evlerinin altına gömmüş olmalı.

Öğleden sonra duvarın dibinde kırmızı boya izleri ve kırık çanak çömlek parçaları bulduk. Duvarda bir zamanlar bir resim olmuş olabilir. Ama izler çok soluk; resim yüzyıllar içinde silinmiş olmalı.

Akşam hoca buluntulara baktı ve şöyle dedi: “Bu evde uzun süre yaşamış olamazlar. Taban yalnızca bir kez sıvanmış. Belki de ev kısa bir süre kullanılmış, sonra terk edilmiş.” Yarın komşu evi açacağız. Orada da bir mezar olup olmadığını çok merak ediyorum.

glossary.en: bottom, foot (duvarın dibi: the foot of the wall)
to fade away, to be wiped off

exercises.translation: Today we cleaned the floor of a house in the south trench. The floor was about a metre below the ground. A small grave came out from under the floor. The bones are very small; they must belong to a child. Next to them there were a stone bead and two small tools. These people must have buried their dead under their houses. In the afternoon we found traces of red paint and broken pieces of pottery at the foot of the wall. There may once have been a painting on the wall. But the traces are very faded; the painting must have worn away over the centuries. In the evening the director looked at the finds and said: “They can't have lived in this house for long. The floor was plastered only once. Perhaps the house was used for a short time, then abandoned.” Tomorrow we'll open the house next door. I really wonder whether there's a grave there too.

questions.q: Whose bones does the writer think they are?
questions.explain: *Bir çocuğa ait olmalı*: **they must belong to a child**.

questions.q: What does the writer conclude from the red traces?
options: There may once have been a painting on the wall
Someone painted the wall last year
questions.explain: *Bir resim olmuş olabilir*: a cautious guess, **may have been**.

questions.q: Why does the director think nobody lived in the house for long?
options: The floor was plastered only once
questions.explain: *Taban yalnızca bir kez sıvanmış*: `-mIş` reports what the evidence shows.
`-mIş olamaz` rules a possibility out: **can't have**.

exercises.text: Elif hâlâ gelmedi. Merak etme, trafiğe ___ olmalı.
exercises.en: Elif still hasn't come. Don't worry, she must have got stuck in traffic.

reject.why: *Olmalı* doesn't follow a finite verb: it follows the participle, *takılmış olmalı*.
*Takılmalı* would be **she must get stuck**, not a guess about the past.

exercises.label: *unutmak*, **must have forgotten**: I must have forgotten, you must have forgotten…
exercises.explain: *Unutmuş* never changes; *olmalı* takes the type I endings, with the buffer y after its last vowel: *olmalıyım*, *olmalıyız*.

accept: He may never have read the letter.
He might never have read the letter.
She [may|might] never have read the letter.
[He|She] [may|might] not have read the letter at all.
exercises.explain: The negative sits on the main verb, inside the guess: *okumamış olabilir*, **may not have read**. *Hiç* makes it **never, not at all**.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **They can't have found the grave**?

why.3: *Bulamamış olabilirler*: **they may not have been able to find it**, only a possibility.

exercises.explain: *Olamaz* after `-mIş` rules the event out: **can't have**.

exercises.task: An archaeologist finds a small clay figure under a house floor, next to a child's grave. Write three or four sentences guessing what it was and why it was there. Use at least three of these: `-mIş olmalı`, `-mIş olabilir`, `-mIş olamaz`, `-mAmIş olabilir`, `-(I)yor olabilir`.
models: Figür çok küçük ve basit; bir oyuncak olabilir. Çocuk onunla oynamış olmalı, ailesi de onu mezara çocuğun yanına koymuş olabilir. Oraya kazara düşmüş olamaz, çünkü tabanın altındaydı.
Figür mezarın hemen yanında bulundu; çocukla birlikte gömülmüş olmalı. Aile onu çocuğu korusun diye koymuş olabilir. Bir tanrıyı gösteriyor da olabilir, ama bunu kesin olarak bilmiyoruz.
checklist: At least three modal forms, each with the person ending on the last word: *koymuş olmalılar*, *oynamış olabilir*
`-mIş olmalı` for what the evidence makes almost certain, `-mIş olabilir` for a possibility
`-mIş olamaz` or `-mAmIş olabilir` to rule something out or doubt it
A reason for each guess, with *çünkü*, `-DIğI için` or *diye*

exercises.explain: Root out: *bul-* (find), *bulun-* (be found: after l the passive is `-In`), *bulunama-* (cannot be found), *bulunamamış*. Add *olmalı*: **it can't have been found**.
